title: Off the Walls of a Circular Room
program_note:
Off the Walls of a Circular Room can be thought of as a series of musical tableaux which follow one another, sometimes obscuring the ends or the beginnings of each other.  In another way, then, this composition can be thought of as a study of figure/ground relationships, an issue crucial in the visual arts but only occasionally discussed in a musical context.  The “room” in which these tableaux are “hung” is termed circular because the music can start at any of five different points other than the beginning and — after reaching the end of the work — continues from near the beginning to a point corresponding to the alternate starting point.

Off the Walls of a Circular Room was written for David Stock and the Pittsburgh New Music Ensemble, and is dedicated to him.  It was written over a period of two months, from October to December, 1996.

David S. Lefkowitz

31 December, 1996

Los Angeles, California
